name: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
problem: Reasoning ability in LLMs has depended on large volumes of human-annotated chains of thought, which does not scale and caps the model's ceiling on hard problems.
mechanism: Pure reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (GRPO) - no human reasoning traces - to incentivize emergent self-reflection, verification and strategy adaptation. Two mechanisms carry the distillation story: (1) the emergent reasoning patterns in R1-Zero come from RL alone, with no SFT cold start, which shows reasoning can be elicited rather than taught; (2) those patterns are then explicitly harvested to distill smaller models. The 1.5B, 7B, 14B, 32B and 70B DeepSeek-R1-Distill models are produced by fine-tuning open base models (Qwen and LLaMA) on ~800k R1-generated samples - NOT by training the base models on the reasoning data themselves.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): the RL-trained model achieves superior performance on verifiable tasks (mathematics, coding competitions, STEM) 'surpassing its counterparts trained via conventional supervised learning on human demonstrations', and the emergent reasoning patterns 'can be systematically harnessed to guide and enhance the reasoning capabilities of smaller models'. No single inference speedup number appears in the abstract - the pay-off is that a 1.5B-70B distilled model reaches reasoning quality that previously required a far larger model, which is the real inference-cost reduction.
